q-129206.name: Question 1
q-129206.problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & -6 \\ 4 & 1 & 4 & -9 \\ 0 & 4 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$
q-129206.worked_solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th rows of $A$ are $-6$, $4$, and $1$, respectively.

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & -6 \\ 4 & 1 & 4 & -9 \\ 0 & 4 & -3 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

So, the answer is $-6+4+1=-1.$

q-73143.problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st and $3$rd rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]

The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st and $3$rd rows of $A$ are $4$ and $-1$, respectively.

$$

So, the answer is $4+(-1)=3.$

q-42005.name: Question 3
q-42005.problem:
Which of the following matrices are in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 9 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
q-42005.worked_solution:
Remember that a matrix is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.
- Each leading entry of a row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is not in row echelon form since ${a}_{32}\ne 0$ (condition  II is violated). 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is not in row echelon form since ${b}_{21}\ne 0$ (condition II is violated). 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 9 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, only $C$ is in row echelon form.

$$
q-129228.worked_solution:
Remember that an augmented matrix is in row echelon form if its coefficient matrix satisfies the following conditions:

- All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the bottom of the matrix.
- Each leading entry of a row is in a column to the right of the leading entry of the row above it.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The matrix $A$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -6 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & -8 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 7 & 0 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $C$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 9 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ are in row echelon form.

q-42373.problem:
Consider the matrix $A$ given below.
Which entries of $A$ could be replaced by $0$ in order to get a matrix in row echelon form?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$
q-42373.worked_solution:
Notice that by replacing ${a}_{32}$, ${a}_{43}$ and ${a}_{44}$ with $0$, we get a matrix in row echelon form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\,⟶\,[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

The other options will not give us a matrix in row echelon form.
